title: In 2,007 mutagenized C. elegans strains, non-coding point mutations near essential genes caused death or sterility under a tenth as often as nonsense mutations, except at splice sites
abstract:
In the nematode C. elegans, single-base mutations in the non-coding DNA around essential genes seldom kill the animal or make it sterile: per mutation, they do this less than a tenth as often as nonsense mutations in the same genes, except at splice signals. This gives a direct, calibrated measure of strong effects in non-coding DNA, which conservation and population data cannot separate from weak effects.

We re-analysed the Million Mutation Project: 2,007 mutagenized strains, each propagated by self-fertilization from single animals to F10, so mutations that kill or sterilize homozygous animals are mostly absent. We compared 839,773 unique mutations with counts expected from a 96-type mutation-rate model. Sites around 3,981 genes that are lethal or sterile after RNA interference ("essential") were compared with sites around 13,655 other tested genes in the same 1-Mb bin and expression quintile. The deficit D is the fraction of expected mutations that is missing. The lethal-equivalent fraction f is D, corrected with synonymous sites, divided by the nonsense value.

Nonsense mutations had D = 0.48 (95% CI 0.44 to 0.52). Canonical splice sites had f = 0.49 (0.34 to 0.63), and highly conserved missense sites (phyloP 4 or more) had f = 0.17 (0.10 to 0.25). UTRs, introns and flanks (13.7 Mb; 106,334 expected mutations) had D = 0.010 (-0.001 to 0.022) and f = 0.00 (-0.04 to 0.06). Accessible promoters and enhancers, operon spacers and conserved non-coding bases had no detectable deficit. In a post hoc test, the 20 bp around trans-splice acceptor junctions, where the spliced-leader RNA joins most mRNAs, had f = 0.39 (0.12 to 0.61; weaker with finer expression strata), and a control window upstream had none. Across 10 analysis variants (for example EMS-only strains), the upper 95% limit of the non-coding f was 0.04 to 0.09; a placebo centred on 0.

Thompson et al. (2013) already reported that outside nonsense mutations the MMP counts are close to expectation; we add calibrated intervals, positive controls, regulatory and conserved classes, and the splice-signal exception. Limits: the bound is a per-site average and does not exclude concentrated effects; laboratory selection removes mainly lethal, sterile and visible effects; summed over 13.7 Mb, the non-coding total is not bounded (-1.3 to 1.8 removed non-coding mutations per removed truncating mutation); one compact genome; mostly G:C to A:T changes; heterozygous blocks could not be excluded.

display.caption: Lethal-equivalent fraction f by site class around 3,981 RNAi-essential genes (main analysis): the deficit of induced mutations in 2,007 MMP strains, relative to non-essential genes in the same 1-Mb bin and expression quintile, corrected with synonymous sites and divided by the nonsense deficit. 0 = no deficit; 1 = removed as often as a nonsense mutation. Dots: estimates; bars: 95% bootstrap intervals (genes; elements and operon spacers: elements). Blue: coding and cis-splice sites; orange: non-coding classes; green: trans-splice acceptor windows (post hoc) and their upstream control.

Robustness of f for the pooled non-coding classes (orange), missense (green) and canonical splice sites (blue) across 10 variants: essential-gene definitions (RNAi; at least 2 RNAi experiments; RNAi and allele; allele only), strata (chromosome x expression; 1-Mb bin only; expression deciles), mutagen subsets and exclusion of the 54 strains with most mutations. Only the variant that ignores expression gives a non-coding f above 0. Bars: 95% bootstrap intervals.

Estimated number of MMP mutations removed by selection around essential genes, by class (corrected deficit x expected count; 95% paired bootstrap intervals). Per site, non-coding mutations are seldom removed, but because non-coding DNA is large (106,334 expected mutations) the total number of removed non-coding mutations is not bounded well: -1.3 to 1.8 per removed truncating mutation.

citations.reason: Million Mutation Project: source of the 2,007 mutagenized strains and their mutation calls. Its Figure 5 already reported that, outside nonsense mutations, observed counts by feature were close to expectation; we quantify and extend this.
MMP variant table (870,227 variants) analysed here.
Describes the MMP parental strain and mutation detection.
Accessible promoter and enhancer annotation (ce11) used for the element analysis.
WormBase (release WS297): genome, gene models, RNAi and allele phenotypes, expression, variation IDs, operons.
WormBase WS297 files (EBI mirror).
UCSC ce11 phyloP 26-way, phastCons 26-way elements, RepeatMasker and simple repeats.
Genome-wide RNAi screen that contributes to the RNAi-essential gene set.
Genome-wide RNAi screen of early embryogenesis that contributes to the RNAi-essential gene set.
Mutation-accumulation lines of Chlamydomonas in which coding but not non-coding mutation counts predicted fitness decline; the closest prior direct test.
Distribution of fitness effects of spontaneous mutations from the same Chlamydomonas lines.
Per-base estimate of regulatory function from CRISPRi screens in human cells, a complementary perturbation measure.
Literature check: test of the mutational-hazard explanation of genome size across 807 animals (candidate approach not chosen).
Fission-yeast transposon screen: growth costs in about 10% of non-coding DNA; our point-mutation data agree that strong effects are concentrated and rare.
Fission-yeast insertion depletion near essential genes mostly in introns and slightly in UTRs and upstream DNA; same essential vs non-essential logic, here applied to point mutations in an animal.
Plasmodium insertion screen with a placebo contrast; we also use a placebo test.
Bacterial insertion screens: intergenic effects mostly through a nearby gene.
Human conserved non-coding bases carry much smaller calibrated variant deficits than conserved coding bases; we find the same contrast for lethal effects in C. elegans.
Human X-chromosome analysis concluding that strong recessive selection acts on few non-coding bases; our homozygous lethality data agree.
Mouse enhancer deletions often show no defect; consistent with the robustness of accessible elements to single-base changes found here.
Rice EMS lines analysed by homozygous vs heterozygous calls; related design, aimed at mutagenesis bias; relevant to our Prediction 4.
